topic.title: Conditional utility of supplied history order
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, does supplied history order improve click AUC beyond the unordered collection of valid historical events, their item fields, actions and task-mask memberships, at justified parameter and measured runtime cost?
topic.hypothesis: The strongest visible model is the inherited utility control; compact evidence does not establish whether supplied order contributes useful information. If it does, removing order while preserving each complete event and its task memberships should reduce click AUC. Compare unchanged order with joint permutations of all historical item fields, actions and task memberships within valid history positions, and with a capacity-matched order-invariant replacement. Preserve padding, event counts, current target, context, host masks and training exposure; do not infer timestamps or elapsed-time effects. Distinguish evaluation-only sensitivity from utility after matched retraining, verify that treatments actually alter order and preserve event associations, and measure parameters and runtime. No reproducible disadvantage after effective order removal would falsify useful order dependence in this setting; evaluation-only degradation could instead reflect distribution shift, while gains could reflect regularization or capacity. Reserve remaining resources for attribution, repetition and authorized assessment before expanding the suite. No novelty or mechanism confirmation is claimed.
